author: Ling Xin,Zhang Tong,Han Li
description:
A Chinese PhD student at Princeton University, New Jersey, was detained by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on Thursday after presenting her research at a neuroscience conference in Washington, the South China Morning Post has confirmed.
Eva Yi Xie, a third-year neuroscience student, was detained at Ronald Reagan National Airport in Washington while travelling home from the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting, according to a post on social media by her lab, the Brody Lab. It...
title: Princeton PhD student from China detained by ICE after US academic conference

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Drawing on lessons from the Ukraine war, Chinese military commentators are calling for frontline commanders to have greater freedom to make battlefield decisions without waiting for orders from above, as drones and AI accelerate the pace of combat.
Since July, several commentaries in the PLA Daily, the People’s Liberation Army’s official newspaper, have proposed ways to delegate tactical authority while keeping major military operations under centralised command.
This type of flexibility...
title: Can China’s top-down military adapt to the speed of AI and drone warfare?

author: Igor Patrick
description:
The US embassy in Mexico accused China on Thursday of supplying Mexican cartels with chemicals used to make methamphetamine, on the same day President Claudia Sheinbaum wrapped up a visit to Shenzhen during which she signed cooperation agreements with Beijing covering energy, science and the environment.
The embassy cited the US Department of Justice in a social media post and referred to chemicals bound for the Sinaloa Cartel that US Homeland Security Investigations seized in September last...
title: US embassy steps up attack on China over cartel meth as Mexico signs deals with Beijing

author: Zhang Tong
description:
US President Donald Trump has tapped the Pentagon’s chief information officer as his new cyber chief following a series of major outages that disrupted air travel, banking and classified communications, saying on Friday that her predecessor was not “good enough”.
Kirsten Davies will serve as acting national cyber director, replacing Sean Cairncross, who was dismissed on Thursday. She would need Senate confirmation to hold the post permanently.
Asked at a White House press conference on Friday...
title: Trump replaces US cyber chief after outages hit flights, banks and NSA

author: Nayan Seth
description:
US President Donald Trump said on Friday that China had agreed to hold trilateral nuclear risk-reduction talks for the first time despite earlier reluctance, as he acknowledged the wide gap between Beijing’s arsenal and the much larger stockpiles held by the US and Russia.
“They didn’t want to do that because China ... is way behind,” Trump said in a press conference at the White House.
“We have estimates of 4,000 nuclear weapons. Russia’s second to us, and China’s way behind. But they’ll catch...
title: Trump says China agreed to trilateral despite reluctance, notes nuclear gap

author: Amber Wang
description:
The joint pledge to reduce nuclear risk by the United States, China and Russia during their unprecedented three-way summit this week sends a positive signal on stability, analysts say, although they warn that there is little room for optimism without concrete measures.
Nuclear arms control among the world’s three major nuclear powers – long sought by US President Donald Trump – failed to make it into the joint declaration after his talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President...
title: Concrete aims or just symbolism? Trump, Xi and Putin talk nuclear risk but controls stall

author: Frank Wilczek
description:
Modern physics recognises four fundamental forces: gravity, electromagnetism and the weak and strong subnuclear forces. (Professional physicists usually speak of “interactions” rather than “forces”, but here I’ll use the more familiar, more vivid alternative.) Each of these forces plays an important role in our description of the world.
Gravity rules the cosmos. Though gravity is extremely feeble at the level of individual particles, it is always attractive, and for astronomical bodies (and for...
title: The real ‘fifth force’: how quantum statistics shapes our world in profound ways

author: Alyssa Chen,Cao Jiaxuan
description:
A rare consensus reached by China, Russia and the US that challenges the authority of international judicial bodies matters for Beijing’s rejection of a 2016 arbitration ruling on the South China Sea, according to analysts.
The joint declaration issued after the unprecedented trilateral summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump on Thursday said the three leaders “recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for...
title: How Beijing’s South China Sea stance benefits from a rare joint warning to the ICC

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China and the United States discussed maritime security this week in talks in Shanghai that ran in parallel to the summit between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump.
Representatives from the People’s Liberation Army Navy hosted officials from US Pacific Command, the Pacific Fleet and Air Force, coastguards and representatives from the Pentagon.
These meetings, which ran from Wednesday to Friday, included “discussions between operators focused on reducing the risk of unsafe and unprofessional...
title: US and China hold maritime security talks in parallel with Xi-Trump meetings

author: Wenran Jiang
description:
The image everyone will remember from Shenzhen is three men in one frame – Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, with Xi at the centre. But the story is not the smiling photos, or even the week. It is the 11 months that produced it. Beijing did not just host a summit. It ran a year-long campaign.
Since last December’s meeting opened the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum’s “China Year”, China has held three senior Apec officials’...
title: China didn’t just host an Apec summit. It ran a year-long campaign

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping urged visiting US President Donald Trump to do “the right thing” on Taiwan this week – a remark experts said suggested a push for further restrictions on US arms sales to the island.
“The US must keep doing the right thing to avoid major setbacks in China-US relations,” Xi told Trump during their bilateral talks on Thursday at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in Shenzhen, according to Beijing’s summary of the meeting.
Trump said the US did not...
title: Xi presses Trump to do ‘the right thing’ on Taiwan. Where does that leave US arms sales?

author: Fan Chen
description:
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr has downplayed Beijing’s choice of music to greet him at the Apec summit, saying the debate about possible hidden meanings was overblown.
A Chinese orchestra played the classic Philippine song “Anak”, which means child, when the Philippine presidential couple entered the hall for the welcome banquet in Shenzhen on Wednesday.
The song, written by Freddie Aguilar, tells the tale of a young person’s rebellion against parental authority and subsequent...
title: It’s just a song: Philippine leader Marcos laughs off debate over Apec welcome track Anak

author: Eve Qiao
description:
Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum’s journey in economy class from Mexico City to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit has gone viral on Chinese social media.
While most world leaders travelled to the southern Chinese city on chartered airliners or government aircraft, Sheinbaum arrived on Monday on a scheduled commercial flight.
She flew on China Southern Airlines flight CZ8032, according to CARNOC, a Chinese aviation trade publication.
The aircraft had a special blue,...
title: Mexican leader Sheinbaum’s 21-hour economy-class journey draws praise in China

author: Raymond Ma,Neil Denslow
description:
An unprecedented trilateral meeting between the leaders of China, the United States and Russia produced a pledge “to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations”. Turning that into a reality is likely to prove a challenge.
The pledge should carry weight, as the US and Russia are two of the world’s largest oil producers while China is the biggest crude importer. Fuel was also second in the four-point agreement reached at the Shenzhen meeting,...
title: China-US-Russia talks, economy concerns, Auto Guangzhou

author: Carol Yang
description:
When Apec leaders assembled in Shenzhen on Thursday for their group photo, they kept up one of the bloc’s traditions by donning traditional garb from the host country.
This time, rather than the more elaborate outfits worn at some previous summits – including the “new Chinese-style” jackets worn the last time China hosted the event – the leaders just slipped on an understated silk scarf over their formal clothing.
In keeping with China’s meticulous approach to major international gatherings,...
title: The subtle symbolism behind the silk scarves worn by the Apec leaders at Shenzhen summit

author: Dewey Sim
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping encouraged China and Singapore to be “development partners that lead in innovation”, urging closer coordination within regional groupings such as the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean).
In talks with Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong on Friday, Xi called the countries “friendly close neighbours” that should deepen strategic communication and strengthen solidarity, according to mainland state news agency Xinhua.
“China and Singapore should be...
title: Xi urges China-Singapore innovation partnership in talks with PM Lawrence Wong

author: Fan Chen
description:
Exchanges between top Chinese and Japanese leaders show Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi adopting a far more proactive approach to assert control and seek direct communication, according to body language experts.
Over the past two days, the Apec gala in Shenzhen has been the scene of rare in-person, high-level interactions between the two countries’ leaders, the most notable since ties between Beijing and Tokyo became severely strained over Takaichi’s remarks regarding Taiwan in November last...
title: 11-second handshake: Takaichi adopts more proactive approach with Xi at Apec, experts say

author: Orange Wang
description:
China and Australia should be “partners that trust each other”, President Xi Jinping told Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Shenzhen on Friday.
Xi struck an upbeat tone on Beijing’s relationship with Canberra, describing it as “developing steadily” now, in the meeting after the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ summit in the southern Chinese city.
“China and Australia have neither historical grievances nor fundamental conflicts of interest, and should be partners who trust...
title: Xi Jinping urges trust-based partnership with Australia in Shenzhen bilateral talks

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. China’s first lady Peng Liyuan lets her English do the talking in Trump welcome
Chinese first lady Peng Liyuan again let her English do the talking as she accompanied President Xi Jinping in welcoming his US counterpart Donald Trump...
title: Comb restores hair growth; Kim Jong-un daughter’s luxury ski gear: SCMP’s 7 highlights

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s absence from the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering in Shenzhen could indicate that a meeting with Donald Trump will not take place in the foreseeable future.
Analysts said it was a vastly different geopolitical and logistical situation from Trump’s first term, when the two leaders met three times.
Sydney Seiler, senior adviser to the Korea chair at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies, said Kim was trying to “lock in” his nuclear weapons...
title: Why the ball is in Kim Jong-un’s court on a meeting with Donald Trump

author: Ben Hu
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a trilateral summit in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. Following the summit, the three sides issued a joint declaration towards peace, including consensus on United Nations reform, global energy supply, sovereign immunity, and nuclear risk reduction.
